title: The first Hodge differential vanishes in characteristic zero
statement:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field] and let $W$ be a smooth projective $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism]. No connectedness or geometric integrality is assumed. Let $\Omega^1_{W/F}$ be the sheaf of Kähler differentials obtained by gluing $\Omega_{A/F}$ on affine opens [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and let $d:\mathcal O_W\to\Omega^1_{W/F}$ be the universal $F$-linear derivation. For every $q\geq0$ the induced map
$$H^q(W,d):H^q(W,\mathcal O_W)\longrightarrow H^q(W,\Omega^1_{W/F})$$
is zero. The induced map is formed in Zariski sheaves of $F$-vector spaces; their cohomology on these sheaves agrees canonically with ordinary module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]. In particular this does not regard $d$ as an $\mathcal O_W$-linear map. The field $F$ need not admit an embedding into $\mathbf C$.

proof.text: Apply the field-model lemma to obtain $k\subseteq F$, $X_0/k$ and $\sigma:k\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, with $X_0\times_kF\cong W$. Put $Y=X_0\times_{k,\sigma}\mathbf C$. Both schemes to which complex comparison will be applied are smooth projective; no geometric integrality or connectedness is used.

source.place: Tags 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), 01ZP (lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation), 0C0C (lemma-descend-smooth), applied to the directed union of finitely generated subfields of F. The complex embedding clause is the elementary transcendence-basis/algebraic-extension argument, expanded in report.md.

proof.text: Fix $q\geq0$ and $a\in H^q(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. The comparison lemma identifies it with a Dolbeault class $c_{0,q}(a)$ on $M=Y^{\mathrm{an}}$. Choose the harmonic representative $\alpha$ supplied by the harmonic-representative lemma. That lemma gives $d_{\mathrm{an}}\alpha=0$. Since $d_{\mathrm{an}}\alpha=\partial\alpha+\bar\partial\alpha$ and the two summands have distinct types, $\partial\alpha=0$. The comparison formula is $c_{1,q}(H^q(Y,d_Y)(a))=[(-1)^q\partial\alpha]=0$. Injectivity of $c_{1,q}$ shows $H^q(Y,d_Y)(a)=0$. As $a$ was arbitrary, $H^q(Y,d_Y)=0$. This works on the finite union of components, including the empty union.

proof.text: Write $u_0=H^q(X_0,d_{X_0})$. Apply the scalar-extension square to $k\xrightarrow{\sigma}\mathbf C$. Its isomorphisms and step 2 show $u_0\otimes_k\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf C}=0$. Scalar extension of vector spaces along a field embedding detects zero maps: if $v=u_0(x)\ne0$, extend $v$ to a basis of its target and let $\lambda$ be the $k$-linear coordinate functional with $\lambda(v)=1$; then $(\lambda\otimes\mathrm{id})(v\otimes1)=1$, contradicting $v\otimes1=0$. Hence $u_0=0$. The coordinate functional uses only elementary linear algebra.

Differential compatibility is the scalar formula d(a tensor lambda)=da tensor lambda and the universal differential base-change isomorphism of lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change; report.md spells out the Cech argument.

proof.text: Apply the same square to $k\hookrightarrow F$. It gives $H^q(X_0\times_kF,d)\circ\beta^q_0=\beta^q_1\circ(u_0\otimes\mathrm{id}_F)=0$. Surjectivity of $\beta^q_0$ makes $H^q(X_0\times_kF,d)=0$. Under the model isomorphism with $W$, the universal derivations agree: on an affine chart a ring isomorphism sends $da$ to the differential of its image, by the universal property. Functoriality of right-derived global sections therefore identifies this zero map with $H^q(W,d)$. Since $q$ was arbitrary this proves the statement; no embedding of $F$ into $\mathbf C$ was chosen.
